name: Sinew-backed bow
notes:
A short bow for horseback and broken ground: a timber belly, sinew glued along the back to take the stretch, antler let into the tips. The sinew is what makes it -- dried, it tightens as it goes, which no plant fibre does, and canon says exactly that on the material itself.

Short because of where it is used. A long bow is drawn standing still on flat ground, and the people who carry these are moving, on slopes, among animals.

Affords `cut` and `deter`, like every other weapon here. Nothing in canon affords killing, and the sling entry says why: the record has slings keeping birds off a crop far more often than it has them doing anything else.
